newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone up more, talk of U.S. presentation.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone up more, talk of U.S. presentation.

text.p: Shares in Vodafone Plc extended their early gains by mid morning on Wednesday, boosted by yesterday's buoyant subscriber figures and ahead of a February presentation to U.S. investors and analysts, traders said.
Traders also said analysts at Merrill Lynch set a year-end price target of 300p on the stock, though further details were not immediately available.

The stock was up 13-1/2p at 274-1/2 by 1052 GMT after earlier rising as high as 276, their highest since September 1995. Trading was busy with volume reaching 9.2 million shares, making it the second most active stock in the UK market.
Analyst Steve Scruton at Credit Lyonnais Laing said yesterday's statement from Vodafone that its international subscribers had passed one million should not have been too much of a surprise.
He pointed out that the company had previously said it had 970,000 international subscribers and the number was growing at some 50,000 a month. "But I guess good news is good news," he said.

SocGen analyst John Tysoe also repeated a "buy" recommendation on Vodafone today in the wake of the subscriber figure, pointing to strong growth in markets such as Hong Kong, South Africa and Greece where it has a franchise.
"The subscriber numbers announced yesterday show the business continues to perform very strongly," Tysoe said. "We have so far only seen the tip of the iceberg."
The SocGen analyst argued that Vodafone had largely missed out on a recent re-rating of independent mobile phone companies in other markets.

And he said that the forthcoming U.S. presentation could help allay fears that Vodafone could suffer in the wake of heavy initial license payments imposed on some new entrants into the U.S. mobile phone market.
"Once the Vodafone management gets in front of U.S. investors we believe the story will look very good," Tysoe said, "and we think the North American investor is going to take to it."
